# Sabra & Co.

> Sabra & Co. is an interior design studio in Colorado Springs, Colorado, led by designer Sabra. Its signature style, Settled Warmth, means warm tones, natural texture and rooms that feel collected over time, designed around how families actually live. The studio offers Virtual Design anywhere in the United States, and Full Service and Architectural Design in Colorado Springs and the Front Range.

## Key facts

- Based in Colorado Springs, Colorado. Serves Colorado Springs, Monument, Pueblo and the greater Front Range in person; Virtual Design is available nationwide.
- Phone: +1 (615) 477-4090. Every inquiry gets a reply within 24 hours, Monday through Saturday.
- Every project starts with a free 20 minute discovery call.
- Packages and consultation fees: Virtual Design $250, Full Service Design $350, Architectural Design $500. The design fee is quoted after the consultation.
- Architectural Design projects typically start around $50,000 all-in and run to $250,000 or more.
- Typical timelines: Virtual Design 4 to 6 weeks; Full Service Design 8 to 12 weeks for one room; Architectural Design or whole home 3 to 6 months.
- Style: warm neutrals (cream, clay, oak, aged brass) instead of cool grays and blue; natural materials like linen, jute, stone, unlacquered brass and real wood; rooms that look collected rather than decorated.
- Profiles: [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/sabraandco), [Pinterest](https://www.pinterest.com/sabraandco), [Google Business Profile](https://share.google/tFaY3r9uAA85MvvEc)

## Design Journal

- [How to make a builder grade home feel like yours](https://www.sabraandcompany.com/builder-grade-home-feel-like-yours.html): A Colorado Springs designer on making a new or builder grade home feel like yours: hardware, wall treatments, bathroom mirrors, fixtures, mixing metals, and the one upgrade worth real money.
- [How to organize a kitchen that stays organized](https://www.sabraandcompany.com/how-to-organize-a-kitchen.html): How to organize a kitchen around the way you actually cook: where each zone belongs, what to do with the corner cabinet and small appliances, and why your system stopped working.
- [What to look for in a new build floor plan](https://www.sabraandcompany.com/new-build-floor-plan-what-to-look-for.html): What to check in a new build floor plan before you sign: entry storage, the walk from the garage to the fridge, closets that waste space, garage room for bins, and whether your own furniture actually fits.
- [How to Choose a Couch That Wears In, Not Out](https://www.sabraandcompany.com/how-to-choose-a-couch-that-wears-in.html): Not all wear is bad wear. Here's how to tell lived-in from worn out, which materials age beautifully, and what to check before you buy your next couch.
- [Interior Designer Cost in Colorado Springs](https://www.sabraandcompany.com/interior-designer-cost-colorado-springs.html): What interior design actually costs in Colorado Springs: typical design fees, furnishing budgets, and what a designer's fee really covers.
- [How to warm up a gray living room](https://www.sabraandcompany.com/warming-up-a-cold-gray-home.html): Why gray rooms feel cold, and the three changes that fix it: curtains, plants and layered lighting. From a Colorado Springs interior designer.
